findings.what: "The neutral carries little" is unsourced and misleads: at the top of row 1 (15%) the neutral carries 45% of the line, 67.50 A of 150 A on screen 3's own slider. Give the sourced reason instead: up to 15%, BS 7671 does not count the neutral as a loaded conductor (Regulation 523.6.1, as NICEIC words it, already cited on this screen), so the line current and a factor of 1.0 stand.

Each calls Ib ÷ 0.86 "the current its cable must be chosen to carry", but screen 4's rule box and the worked example (his slides p.36) divide In, together with Ca and Cg. Add one line on screen 8: this is the Appendix 4 and Schneider guide's "design load"; once a device is chosen, In takes Ib's place in It ≥ In ÷ (Ca × Cg × 0.86) (lesson 8), so 9.56 A is a floor, not the It the cable is finally chosen on.

The words say the 120° between the lines is one whole cycle of the ripple, but the picture never draws it. A small bracket over the L1 and L2 traces spanning 120°, labelled "120° = one ripple cycle", would make the cause visible as well as the result.

findings.where: Screen 3 at 360 px, light and dark (moved shots)
findings.what: The held sentence keeps room for its longest wording, leaving about three blank lines between "…sets the cable." and the readouts. The harness also warns "page height keeps growing with the frame at 340 px". Tighten the longest wording, or let the readouts sit higher.

findings.where: Screen 3, the Line bar and Table 4Aa strip
findings.what: The Line bar fills mint green (k-fill3) and the active Table 4Aa band fills amber (k-fill2). In the D4 palette, green means finished and amber means key terms or what is due, so use ink or grey for both and keep red for the neutral passing the line.

findings.where: Screen 3, entering it again with Back
findings.what: The demonstration restarts from 0% every time he comes back to the screen, which overwrites a setting he dragged to. Start it only on the first visit and leave Replay for the rest.

findings.where: Screen 1, the right-answer feedback before Skip to the practice
findings.what: The recall tests only Ibn = 3 × h × IL, but the skip also passes Table 4Aa's rows, which part (e) needs. Add the row to the right feedback ("35% is row 3: the neutral current, factor 0.86") so the skip carries what (e) asks.
Why? can be pressed before any pick and prints the full working with the answer (150.00 A), so it can give the check away. Show it only after the first pick (i1 has the same pattern).

The panel carries (a) and (b) and then asks (d), so the question's lettering jumps over (c), the installation's maximum demand (160.44 A, lesson 2). Carry 3c too, or say that (c) is on the course page, as a C&G paper would.

The figures given "for scale" are THD (Philips under 20%, ANSI 32%), and screen 4 has just said THD is not the third harmonic. The case file's IEC 61000-3-2 Class C third-harmonic limit for lighting (30 × the circuit power factor, %) is a third-harmonic figure and a fairer scale for the practice 20%, if its quote is on file.

His slides consider harmonics only when the maker's data states one (p.37), and here no datasheet exists. Say so in one line ("on the job, no maker's figure means none is applied; this part shows the method on a practice value") so the practice 20% does not read against his own slide.

This is the densest screen: an opening paragraph, four row buttons, the row's why, the rule box, then a paragraph of about 90 words on the maker's figure (THD, two makers, a motor with no neutral). Move the maker's-figure paragraph to screen 7, where the 20% is used, or into its own short block.

findings.where: Screen 9, Section B written b1, need
findings.what: "Any three" of the five points can be met with points 1 to 3 alone, which never reach the question's second half, "what that means for the cable". Make need "any three, including point 4 or 5".

findings.where: Screen 11, Keep this card, The showroom so far
findings.what: Figure 3d is marked as being on the practice 20%, but 3b and 3e, also built on practice values (practice: true in the case file), carry no mark. Tag each practice-built figure. Also "Where it lives: Your slides…" should take a lower-case "your".

findings.where: Lesson JSON practice text (the Book), step 4 of the method
findings.what: "Read the column for three or four loaded cables" misstates Table 4D1A column 5, whose heading is three or four cables, three-phase a.c. (three loaded). Drop "loaded", since the whole point of Table 4Aa is that a loaded fourth conductor is not what the column assumes.
